reviews.title: Worth every dollar
reviews.text:
TLDR: Brick is simple in both function and form. It's done what other blocking apps haven't, and makes my phone a tool and not a mind-numbing time-sucking addiction. It's also a one-time purchase and not yet another subscription. I consider the price of the Brick device a clever way these guys devised to get people to pay what a quality app and on going maintenance is worth.
———
I’ve tried Screentime, Freedom, and AppBlock. Screentime is a joke. Freedom and AppBlock each have pros and cons, including glitches where they'd sometimes work and sometimes not. What Brick has that none of these have is simplicity and a physical device.

The design is dark, boring, and plain, *which is exactly what these apps should be*. My desire is to stay off my phone, not get sucked into a brightly colored app with a statistics tab that I manage to waste 25 minutes on and have so many blocking options that scheduling them can act like a minor hobby. The statistics tab just shows you how long your phone was Bricked vs not Bricked. The scheduling options are either a blocklist or an allowlist and the day(s) and time(s) you want it active.

There's only one mode and the only way to turn it off is to tap my phone to a physical plastic square. This works *so well*. In most situations, that's enough to keep me from unbricking. I just really don't want to get up and walk across the kitchen or down the stairs in order to scroll Reddit. If I delete the app in order to turn off a session, I need to set everything up again when I reinstall it. There are only five emergency unbricks and I don't want to use one because I just had to watch YouTube while brushing my teeth. It also has yet to glitch and give me access when I shouldn't or block me when I should have access.

The only downside I've seen is if I forget to unbrick before I leave the house to go somewhere. But then again, do I REALLY need to ask ChatGPT if this new product at Costco is any good, check my email when standing in line, or order something from Amazon *that instant*? (No.)

This is actually helping me reconfigure my relationship to my phone and I barely have to think about it. It just works quietly in the background.

(I also like that this supports a small business in my home state.)

reviews.title: Helps with ADHD
reviews.text:
I have had the Brick for about three weeks so far and it has immediately helped me with lowering my screen time amount. 

It's night and day from when I'm using Brick to when I'm not. I often end up binging content when I'm not using Brick or I end up using the phone mindlessly when I'm not using Brick versus when I am. 

I'm thinking more about screen time because when I go to certain apps it's like, "Ah this app is locked. Get back to enjoying life” I have to do something physically to unlock it, right? I have to go to the kitchen and tap on the Brick or have to go get it out of my bag and tap on it. That small barrier is enough for me to slow down and be like, "Okay I don't need this right now. I can focus on something else."

That has been a huge plus for me when it comes to using this device because ADHD thrives on external motivators. 

Sometimes I'm just in the habit of being curious about, "What's this person saying about this thing going on in the world?" or "What's this person saying about that?" Having that barrier to remind me, "No, wake up and get your routine started and then make a conscious choice about when you're going to use social media and why you're going to use it and how." After about two weeks of using it I would say I'm enjoying it.

reviews.title: Great
reviews.text: I really like this and find it way more effective than screen time apps. Putting the brick in another room really does a lot to overcome the impulse to ignore screen time limits. Also, I always wanted to ignore my phone more but loved listening to music and white noise and always needed to use stuff like the notes app or GPS, so it was hard to turn it off or leave it at home. This solves all my problems!!!

reviews.title: Worth it!
reviews.text:
Honestly, I’ve tried a handful of other apps. They work for a while and then I’m back to my old ways because they are too easy to bypass. Let’s be real—it’s an addiction & we’ll find a way to get our fix.

I believe the biggest game changer is having to physically move my body to unlock my phone. 

Example: 

I have to actively choose to walk away from playing with my child to unlock my phone. That’s a wild realization to find yourself in. & the sad reality is that without Brick I was doing that. I’d get sucked into a doom scroll, start researching ‘this’ or ‘that’, window -shop for things we need at home, etc.

Now I have my dedicated phone time where I can do all of that, but I also have my dedicated ’be present’ time. I’m sleeping better, my quality time with the people I love has improved, and I’m re-learning that it’s okay to not have all of the answers right at my fingertips + actually using my mind! 

Highly recommend Brick!

reviews.title: Extremely helpful but incomplete
reviews.text: Putting myself on a schedule has been extremely helpful and has allowed me to get back much of my day. My only disappointment with the app is that there is no way to set a time limit for an app. For instance, I like to wake up and catch up on the news. The problem is that I’ll frequently go down rabbit holes and what I was hoping to be a 20 to 30 minute update on the state of the world turns into 90 minutes to 2 hours. I’d really love to set my news app for a 20 or 30 minute time limit and have it brick after that much like screen time does. Currently, I have to decide whether I want to read the news at all or risk wasting a good portion of my morning.

reviews.title: Please bring back timed brick sessions!
reviews.text:

And be in control of timing myself out for 30 minutes when necessary. 

My favorite part was NOT having to create the neuropath way of “unbricking” my phone. Now that the timed sessions are gone, it feels way less impactful.  Because I am forced to unbrick(instead of letting a timer run out) I am developing a bad habit of unbricking it at all times. I can’t keep my brick in a safe, It defeats the purpose I bought it for. 

I’ve talked to several friends who feel the exact same. So disappointed. I know so many customers feel this, please consider adding this feature back. It was life changing and my mental health was in peak condition when I had timed sessions🙏 

I know you’ll probably respond to this with some explanation on how you’re here to serve what’s best or whatever. But PLEASE just CONSIDER adding it back. That’s all I ask. Thank you!

reviews.title: Easy to use and it works!
reviews.text: I find that Brick is straightforward, easy to use, and not at all overwhelming! For me, the best part is the physical component. Once the set schedule ends, you have to actually get up and tap the phone to unlock it. Since it isn’t a passive timer that just hands back access, I find that this preserves our autonomy as adults. That simple physical act reminds us that the phone is just a tool under our control and I feel that it builds a genuine sense of discipline and self-efficacy which is what we need in order to have a healthy long term relationship with our phone.

reviews.title: Best option out there

Also, I used to use the “Brick for X amount of time” feature a lot. It’s seems to have been removed. Please if you could add it back or make accessing it more obvious. This has been my only gripe. The use case is. It fulfilled by the schedule feature.

This was the main selling point for me - the ability to only allow a 5-10 apps and websites, and block everything else - but this doesn’t work.

Customer support was quick and friendly, but unfortunately I don’t know of any solutions yet. Hoping to see an update soon!

reviews.title: Great overall, one suggestion/request
reviews.text:
This app and the associated device has made significant improvements to my life. I no longer doom scroll in the mornings, during work, or in the afternoons. I even set up a schedule to block shopping apps after 7:30pm as I noticed that is when I am the most likely to make impulse purchases.

One thing that I think could really elevate this is to add the option for notifications to suggest bricking the device if a certain app has been in use for a while. For example, users could flag instagram as an app that, if they’ve been using it for more than 20 minutes consecutively, brick will send a notification asking if they’d like to brick their device. Not automatically bricking it, but just a notification of “hey, maybe you’re doomscrolling, want us to put an end to it?” I know for me that would be incredibly helpful when for times I haven’t even noticed I’ve been doomscrolling.

reviews.text:

With Brick, that couldn't be further from the case. It's the first product I've used where it's been totally worth it. Its impact is direct and noticeable if used correctly and you'll find yourself breaking habits easily. I wish they had a product for weight loss. 

A tip: if you have a house with multi levels ask your spouse or loved one to hide the brick on the opposite floor. That way if you really need to unbrick - you have someone you trust who can share a location. 

If you're in the fence about the product - buy it. It's excellent.

I find I don’t need to look at many things during the day and it can *almost* always wait. I love the removal of urgency without being permanently blocked out by time limits (my spouse has the screen time password). If I delete apps I eventually reinstall them when I do need important info. The ability to brick the App Store is amazing because I’m a screen junkie who will download infinite browsers just to get an unlimited fix of YouTube. I’ll even scroll through reviews just to have something to scroll through. Amazing device.

10/10 would buy again.

Update: 05/17. They fixed the scheduling issues that were originally happening and it was going well for a couple of months. However, now the scheduling issues are back in full force. This time the brick won’t unbrick when it is scheduled to. Thankfully I haven’t been out of town or away from home when this has happened, but it’s highly unfortunate that this is happening again. This is the whole point of having the brick. To have something that automatically takes away some of the self control it takes to walk away from your phone or to not log into your apps. That’s  why the schedules exist in the first place. The work around I have found if this happens to you is turning your phone on and off again if it has been bricked for longer than it was scheduled to. I have tried updating the times it is scheduled to brick like customer service recommended last time and that hasn’t worked. Deducting a star for so many inconsistencies and the main points of the app never working as intended. 

Original Review:
The brick has really helped me with my doom scrolling. However, the scheduling portion of the app rarely works. I’ve reached out to support and they recommended to change the schedules and that engineers have an update coming in the new year to hopefully fix it. I’ve changed the schedules as instructed and still run into issues of it either not turning on brick mode when it’s set to or not blocking all the apps it’s supposed to. Hopefully they’re able to fix it, because it is a huge let down as I really rely on the schedules to help break my scrolling habits. Otherwise, it’s great and highly recommend.

reviews.text:
I love my Brick and the way it helps me disconnect so I can focus at work or when I’m trying to be present in my personal life. The option to set timeframes on certain days is amazing, especially when I’m anticipating the need for undivided attention on something.

It’s easy to doom scroll and not realize how long I’ve been doing it, so I would love to see “time limits” become an option. For example, if my screen time on a certain app reaches more than 2 hours in a day, I’d like to be locked out by Brick to encourage me to put my time elsewhere! This was an option with another screen time app I have used before, so I know it can be done.

Regardless, I really love Brick so far and I’m happy with my purchase. I hope to see more features soon!

reviews.title: LOVE IT
reviews.text: Having Brick has helped me cut down on my social media usage so much. I found myself constantly scrolling and wasting so much time. Now that i have a physical blocker i am more conscious with my usage and am getting more done!

reviews.title: I recommend to all my friends!
reviews.text: I swear my friends and fam think I sponsor this app but I really just love it. The way I can’t get out of brick mode (I don’t own a brick device) is so great!! I would always turn the timer off that I have through my phone but this one helps me keep my morning present and off the phone. Sets a great tone for the day. Less doomscrolling :)

reviews.title: Brick? Check!✅
reviews.text: This tool has been great. Working in maintenance requires a lot of time learning systems, as well as maintaining them at our facility. Being “Brick’d” throughout the work day has revived what life was like without a phone as a distraction; it has been so nice! Eventually, I feel natural habits will form from using Brick. Great idea, and highly recommend!

reviews.title: The best I’ve ever seen
reviews.text:
Wow! 🤯🔥🙏
I’m so Impressed. Day 1. Five hours without the social media BS. Let’s see how far it goes.

reviews.title: It’s good but….
reviews.text: It’s great, but there are a few core product issues that make it pretty frustrating. There needs to be a way to specify proximity to brick, so you can unbrick without penalty if you forget to unbrick before leaving home. Also the mechanics of the emergency unbrick are completely ridiculous. You should be able to set number of emergency unbricks, and reset manually. Or they could charge you to emergency unbrick. Having to email and wait for a reset screams poor core business ops.

reviews.title: Life changing
reviews.text: The Brick has done wonders for me. I was skeptical at first but it truly has helped me so much. I’ve had it a few weeks now and my screen time is down over 40%. If you’re on the fence, I urge you to give it a chance.

reviews.title: Best for distractions
reviews.text: Extremely easy to use and keeps you away from your apps. Love having it around.

reviews.title: The only thing that gets me off of my phone
reviews.text:
I have been loving my brick and reclaiming entire days worth of time back. 
My one hang up is that I thought you just had to tap your phone on the brick but you actually have to open the app, press a button and then tap the brick. But still… life changing!

reviews.title: Do it
reviews.text: Stop waiting it works. Cheaper than a “dumb” phone and you don’t realize how much you “quickly scroll for just a minute “ till you can’t anymore.

reviews.title: Excellent!
reviews.text: I typically never write reviews, but Brick has got it figured out! This is by far the most effective tool at reducing my screen time and they keep adding features that make it better! I really appreciate the continuous improvement. Would highly recommend to anybody struggling with phone addiction.

reviews.title: Actually helps!
reviews.text: This actually helps me focus and the physical aspect is a game changer. I also really appreciate the schedule feature so it automatically does it for me.

reviews.title: Works for real life reality situations
reviews.text: Helps me when I can’t help myself

reviews.title: Enjoying more time with my kids
reviews.text: I struggle with social media and being on my phone when I want to be spending time with my kids. Picking up my phone to turn the AC on or checking who is at the door or looking at quick email also means an easy click on any of the social media apps that leads to then holding my time hostage. I’m so thankful for brick and allowing me to get the time with my family back!

reviews.title: I have my life back
reviews.text: I didn’t realize how much social media was *really* taking from me until I started to use Brick. I had tried all of the other methods before and this one is the first one to work for me. Screen time, social media, phone pick ups all decreased radically 😊
